stem.en: Which alkane cannot be prepared by the Wurtz reaction?

explanation.en: Wurtz joins two alkyl groups, so the product has at least two carbons; methane cannot form.

stem.en: Heating sodium propanoate with soda lime gives:

explanation.en: Decarboxylation removes one carbon: CH₃CH₂COONa + NaOH → CH₃CH₃ + Na₂CO₃.

stem.en: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?

explanation.en: Branching reduces surface area and van der Waals forces; straight-chain n-pentane boils highest (309 K).

stem.en: The volume of O₂ needed to burn 2 L of butane completely, at the same temperature and pressure, is:

explanation.en: C₄H₁₀ + 13/2 O₂ → 4CO₂ + 5H₂O. By Avogadro's law, 2 L butane needs 2 × 6.5 = 13 L O₂.

solution.en: By Avogadro's law, 2 L butane needs 2 × 6.5 = 13 L O₂.

stem.en: How many structurally different monochloro products are formed on chlorination of 2-methylbutane (ignore stereoisomers)?

explanation.en: 1-chloro-2-methylbutane, 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, 2-chloro-3-methylbutane and 1-chloro-3-methylbutane: 4.

stem.en: The conformations of ethane arise from:

options.en: rotation about the C–C σ bond

explanation.en: Free rotation about the C–C σ bond changes the relative positions of the hydrogens without breaking any bond.

stem.en: The dihedral angle between the C–H bonds on adjacent carbons in the staggered conformation of ethane is:

explanation.en: In a Newman projection of the staggered form, front and back hydrogens are 60° apart.

stem.en: The most stable conformation of ethane is:

explanation.en: In the staggered form the bond pairs are farthest apart, so torsional strain is least.

stem.en: The energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane is about:

explanation.en: The barrier is about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹, far smaller than a C–C bond energy (~347 kJ mol⁻¹).

solution.en: The barrier is about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹, far smaller than a C–C bond energy (~347 kJ mol⁻¹).

stem.en: Which statement about the staggered and eclipsed forms of ethane is correct?

options.en: They differ in C–C bond length
They differ in H–C–H bond angle
They differ only in dihedral angle and can be separated at room temperature
They differ only in dihedral angle and cannot be separated at room temperature

explanation.en: Bond lengths and angles are the same; only the dihedral angle differs. The low barrier lets them interconvert rapidly, so they cannot be isolated.

stem.en: The major product of propene with HBr (no peroxide) is:

explanation.en: Markovnikov addition via the more stable secondary carbocation puts Br on C2.

stem.en: Ozonolysis of but-2-ene followed by Zn/H₂O gives:

options.en: one molecule each of methanal and propanal

explanation.en: CH₃CH=CHCH₃ is cut at the double bond into two CH₃CHO.

stem.en: Which alkene shows geometrical (cis–trans) isomerism?

explanation.en: In but-2-ene each double-bond carbon carries two different groups (H and CH₃). The others have two identical groups on one carbon.

stem.en: Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide to give mainly:

explanation.en: The peroxide (Kharash) effect gives anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr through a free-radical path.

solution.en: The peroxide (Kharash) effect gives anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr through a free-radical path.

stem.en: An alkene C₅H₁₀ on ozonolysis gives a mixture of propanone and ethanal. The alkene is:

explanation.en: Joining (CH₃)₂C= (from propanone) and =CHCH₃ (from ethanal) gives (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃, 2-methylbut-2-ene.

stem.en: Calcium carbide reacts with water to give:

explanation.en: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → HC≡CH + Ca(OH)₂.

stem.en: Which is the most acidic?

explanation.en: The sp carbon of ethyne has 50% s-character and holds the anion's electron pair best.

stem.en: The number of σ and π bonds in ethyne is:

explanation.en: Two C–H σ bonds plus one C–C σ = 3 σ; the triple bond has 2 π.

stem.en: Propyne on hydration with dilute H₂SO₄ and HgSO₄ gives:

explanation.en: Markovnikov addition of water gives the enol CH₃C(OH)=CH₂, which tautomerises to CH₃COCH₃.

solution.en: Markovnikov addition of water gives the enol CH₃C(OH)=CH₂, which tautomerises to CH₃COCH₃.

stem.en: Which of the following reacts with sodamide to form a sodium salt?

explanation.en: Only a terminal alkyne (with H on the sp carbon) is acidic enough. But-2-yne has no such hydrogen.

stem.en: The electrophile in the nitration of benzene is:

explanation.en: Conc. H₂SO₄ protonates HNO₃, which loses water to form the nitronium ion, NO₂⁺.

stem.en: Which of the following is aromatic?

explanation.en: Benzene is planar, cyclic and conjugated with 6 π electrons (4n + 2, n = 1). Cyclooctatetraene has 8 π electrons and is not planar.

stem.en: Which group is meta-directing in electrophilic substitution?

explanation.en: –NO₂ withdraws electrons by −R and −I, deactivating the ring most at ortho/para, so substitution goes meta.

stem.en: Chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic substitution:

explanation.en: Cl withdraws electrons by −I (deactivating) but its lone pairs donate by +R to ortho/para positions, which directs the attack there.

solution.en: Cl withdraws electrons by −I (deactivating) but its lone pairs donate by +R to ortho/para positions, which directs the attack there.

stem.en: Which of the following species is aromatic?

explanation.en: The cyclopentadienyl anion is planar, cyclic and fully conjugated with 6 π electrons. The cation has 4 π; cyclopentadiene and cycloheptatriene have an sp³ carbon, so they are not fully conjugated.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Addition of HBr to propene in the presence of an organic peroxide gives 1-bromopropane as the main product.
Reason (R): In the presence of peroxide, the addition takes place by a free-radical mechanism, through the more stable secondary radical.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both true; R explains A. The Br• radical adds to the terminal carbon to give the more stable secondary radical CH₃ĊHCH₂Br, which then takes H from HBr: anti-Markovnikov product, 1-bromopropane (peroxide effect).

passage.en: A student is given an unknown alkene with molecular formula C₅H₁₀. To identify it, she carries out ozonolysis (O₃ followed by Zn/H₂O). The products are identified as propanone (CH₃COCH₃) and ethanal (CH₃CHO).

stem.en: What is the unknown alkene?

explanation.en: Join the two carbonyl carbons with a C=C: (CH₃)₂C=O + O=CHCH₃ → (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃, which is 2-methylbut-2-ene. Pent-2-ene would give ethanal and propanal; the but-1-enes would give methanal.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Toluene undergoes nitration faster than benzene.
Reason (R): The methyl group increases the electron density of the benzene ring.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both true; R explains A. Through +I effect and hyperconjugation, –CH₃ makes the ring richer in electrons, so it attacks the electrophile NO₂⁺ faster than benzene does (activating group).

passage.en: A teacher writes Hückel's conditions for aromaticity on the board: the species must be cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and contain (4n + 2) π electrons. She then gives the class three species: the cyclopentadienyl anion (C₅H₅⁻, planar, 6 π electrons), the cyclopropenyl cation (C₃H₃⁺, planar, 2 π electrons) and cyclo-octatetraene (C₈H₈, tub-shaped and non-planar, 8 π electrons).

stem.en: Which of the three species are aromatic?

options.en: The cyclopentadienyl anion and the cyclopropenyl cation

explanation.en: C₅H₅⁻ has 6 π electrons (n = 1) and C₃H₃⁺ has 2 π electrons (n = 0), and both are planar and conjugated: aromatic. Cyclo-octatetraene has 8 π electrons (4n) and is not planar, so it is not aromatic.

stem.en: Which of the following statements about the addition of HBr to propene are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.en: Without peroxide, the major product is 2-bromopropane
In the presence of benzoyl peroxide, the major product is 1-bromopropane
The peroxide effect is also observed with HCl
Markovnikov addition goes through the more stable secondary carbocation

explanation.en: Ionic addition gives the 2° carbocation and 2-bromopropane (Markovnikov). With peroxide, HBr adds by a free-radical chain to give 1-bromopropane (Kharash effect). The peroxide effect is not seen with HCl or HI.

stem.en: Which of the following species are aromatic? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: Benzene (6 π, n = 1), naphthalene (10 π, n = 2) and the planar cyclopentadienyl anion (6 π) obey Hückel's rule. Cyclooctatetraene has 8 π electrons and is tub-shaped (non-planar), so it is not aromatic.

stem.en: How many structurally different monochloro products are possible when 2-methylbutane is chlorinated in light? Give an integer.

explanation.en: 2-Methylbutane, (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₃, has four kinds of hydrogen: the two equivalent CH₃ on C2 (C1), the CH at C2, the CH₂ at C3 and the CH₃ at C4. So 4 structural monochloro products.

stem.en: What mass of calcium carbide, in grams, is needed to produce 2.27 L of ethyne at STP? Give your answer to one decimal place (CaC₂ = 64 g mol⁻¹; molar volume at STP = 22.7 L).

explanation.en: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂. Ethyne = 2.27/22.7 = 0.1 mol, so CaC₂ = 0.1 mol = 6.4 g.

stem.en: The energy difference between the eclipsed and staggered conformations of ethane is about:

explanation.en: The torsional barrier of ethane is only about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹, so rotation about the C–C bond is almost free at room temperature.

solution.en: The torsional barrier of ethane is only about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹, so rotation about the C–C bond is almost free at room temperature.

stem.en: Which of the following groups on a benzene ring directs an incoming electrophile to the meta position?

explanation.en: –NO₂ withdraws electrons by −I and −R and deactivates the ortho and para positions most, so substitution goes meta. –OH, –CH₃ and –Cl are ortho/para directors.

solution.en: –NO₂ withdraws electrons by −I and −R and deactivates the ortho and para positions most, so substitution goes meta. –OH, –CH₃ and –Cl are ortho/para directors.

stem.en: Propyne reacts with water in the presence of dilute H₂SO₄ and HgSO₄ to give mainly:

explanation.en: Water adds by Markovnikov's rule to give the enol CH₃C(OH)=CH₂, which tautomerises to the ketone CH₃COCH₃.

stem.en: Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. The major product is:

explanation.en: Peroxide switches the mechanism to free-radical addition (Kharasch effect). Br• adds to the terminal carbon to give the more stable 2° radical, so Br ends up on C1: anti-Markovnikov product 1-bromopropane.

stem.en: Ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene followed by Zn/H₂O workup gives:

explanation.en: 2-Methylbut-2-ene is (CH₃)₂C=CH–CH₃. Cleaving the C=C gives (CH₃)₂C=O (propanone/acetone) and CH₃CHO (ethanal/acetaldehyde).

stem.en: Which compound gives a white precipitate with ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent)?

explanation.en: Only terminal alkynes have an acidic ≡C–H (sp carbon, 50% s character). But-1-yne forms silver butynide; but-2-yne has no acetylenic hydrogen.

stem.en: A mixture of CH₃Br and C₂H₅Br is treated with sodium in dry ether. The products formed are:

explanation.en: In the Wurtz reaction any two alkyl groups can couple: CH₃–CH₃ (ethane), CH₃–C₂H₅ (propane) and C₂H₅–C₂H₅ (butane). That is why Wurtz is poor for making odd-carbon alkanes.

stem.en: In the nitration of benzene with a mixture of conc. HNO₃ and conc. H₂SO₄, the attacking electrophile is:

explanation.en: H₂SO₄ protonates HNO₃, which loses water to form the nitronium ion NO₂⁺, a strong electrophile.

stem.en: The most stable conformation of n-butane (about the C2–C3 bond) is:

explanation.en: In the anti conformation the two CH₃ groups are 180° apart, minimising both torsional strain and steric repulsion. Fully eclipsed is the least stable.

stem.en: On free-radical monochlorination, 2-methylbutane can give how many structurally different monochloro products?

explanation.en: 2-Methylbutane: (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₃. Distinct H environments: the two equivalent CH₃ on C2, the C2–H, the C3–H₂, and the C4–H₃. That gives 4 structural isomers (two of them, from chlorinating C1 and C3, are chiral).

stem.en: Which of the following alkanes cannot be prepared by the Wurtz reaction?

explanation.en: The Wurtz reaction joins two alkyl groups: $2\text{R–X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R–R} + 2\text{NaX}$, so the product always has at least two carbons. Ethane comes from $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$, butane from $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$ and 2,3-dimethylbutane from 2-bromopropane. Methane (one carbon) cannot be made this way.

stem.en: A mixture of $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$ is treated with sodium in dry ether. The products are:

explanation.en: Coupling can occur CH₃–CH₃ (ethane), CH₃–C₂H₅ (propane) and C₂H₅–C₂H₅ (butane). Because a mixture is hard to separate, the Wurtz reaction is used to make symmetrical alkanes with an even number of carbons from a single halide.

stem.en: In Kolbe's electrolysis of an aqueous solution of sodium propanoate, the hydrocarbon obtained and the electrode at which it forms are:

explanation.en: At the anode, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$ loses an electron and $\text{CO}_2$ to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^{\bullet}$; two such radicals combine to give butane, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$. Hydrogen is released at the cathode. Ethane would come from sodium ethanoate.

stem.en: How many structurally different monochloro products can be obtained by free-radical chlorination of 2-methylbutane? (Ignore stereoisomers.)

explanation.en: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}{-}\text{CH}_2{-}\text{CH}_3$ has four kinds of H: the two equivalent $\text{CH}_3$ on C2, the C2–H, the C3 $\text{CH}_2$, and the C4 $\text{CH}_3$. Products: 1-chloro-2-methylbutane, 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, 2-chloro-3-methylbutane, 1-chloro-3-methylbutane = 4.

stem.en: In free-radical chlorination at room temperature, the relative reactivity per hydrogen atom is 3° : 2° : 1° = 5 : 3.8 : 1. What percentage of the monochloro product from 2-methylpropane is 2-chloro-2-methylpropane? (Give your answer to one decimal place.)

explanation.en: 2-Methylpropane, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CH}$, has 1 tertiary H and 9 primary H. Relative amounts: tertiary $1 \times 5 = 5$; primary $9 \times 1 = 9$. % tertiary chloride $= 5/(5+9) \times 100 = 35.7\%$. Ignoring the number of H atoms would wrongly give 5/6 = 83%; ignoring reactivity gives 10%.

stem.en: Iodination of alkanes is carried out in the presence of an oxidising agent such as $\text{HIO}_3$ or $\text{HNO}_3$ because:

explanation.en: HI is a strong reducing agent and converts $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ back to $\text{CH}_4$. Oxidising the HI (e.g. $5\text{HI} + \text{HIO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{I}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$) removes it and drives the equilibrium forward.

options.en: it oxidises the HI formed, preventing the reverse reaction
it generates iodine free radicals as a catalyst
it increases the electronegativity of iodine
it dissolves iodine in the alkane

stem.en: In the free-radical chlorination of methane, which step is a chain-termination step?

explanation.en: Termination steps consume radicals without making new ones — two radicals combine. Homolysis of Cl₂ is initiation; the two steps that use one radical and produce another are propagation.

stem.en: n-Heptane heated at 773 K and 10–20 atm over $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$/$\text{Mo}_2\text{O}_3$ supported on alumina gives mainly:

explanation.en: This is aromatisation (dehydrogenation + cyclisation). Six of the seven carbons form the benzene ring and the seventh remains as –CH₃, giving toluene. n-Hexane gives benzene. Isomerisation to branched alkanes needs anhydrous AlCl₃/HCl.

stem.en: The energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane is approximately:

explanation.en: The eclipsed form is about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹ higher in energy because of torsional strain (repulsion between C–H bond pairs on adjacent carbons). The staggered form, with a dihedral angle of 60°, is the most stable.

stem.en:
Statement I: The staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane cannot be isolated at room temperature.
Statement II: The energy barrier to rotation about the C–C bond is small enough to be crossed by thermal collisions at room temperature.

explanation.en: With a barrier of only about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹, molecules interconvert between conformations millions of times per second at 298 K, so no single conformer can be separated. Both statements are correct.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Which of the following alkenes shows geometrical (cis–trans) isomerism?

explanation.en: Each doubly bonded carbon must carry two different groups. In but-2-ene, each carbon has H and $\text{CH}_3$. In but-1-ene, propene and 2-methylpropene, one alkene carbon carries two identical groups ($=\text{CH}_2$ or $=\text{C(CH}_3)_2$).

stem.en: Which statement comparing cis- and trans-but-2-ene is correct?

explanation.en: In the cis isomer the C–CH₃ bond dipoles add up to a small net dipole, so it has stronger intermolecular forces and boils higher (≈ 277 K vs 274 K). In the trans isomer the dipoles cancel (μ = 0), but its symmetry lets it pack better in the crystal, so it melts higher.

options.en: The cis isomer has the higher boiling point and the lower melting point
The trans isomer has the larger dipole moment
The cis isomer has the higher melting point
Both have the same boiling point

stem.en: But-2-yne is hydrogenated with H₂ over palladium on barium sulphate partially poisoned with quinoline (Lindlar's catalyst). The product is:

explanation.en: Lindlar's catalyst stops reduction at the alkene stage, and H₂ adds to one face of the triple bond (syn addition), giving the cis-alkene. Na in liquid NH₃ gives the trans-alkene; ordinary Pt/Pd/Ni would continue to butane.

stem.en:
Match the reaction in Column I with its product or type in Column II.
Column I: (P) but-2-yne + H₂, Pd/BaSO₄ + quinoline (Q) but-2-yne + Na/liquid NH₃ (R) 2,3-dibromobutane + Zn dust (S) 2-bromobutane + alcoholic KOH
Column II: (i) trans-but-2-ene (ii) cis-but-2-ene (iii) dehalogenation (iv) dehydrohalogenation

explanation.en: Lindlar → cis (syn addition); Na/liq NH₃ (dissolving-metal reduction) → trans. Zn removes both Br atoms of a vicinal dibromide (dehalogenation), while alcoholic KOH removes HBr (dehydrohalogenation, β-elimination). Swapping P and Q is the classic error.

stem.en: The major product of the addition of HBr to propene (no peroxide) is:

explanation.en: Markovnikov's rule: H adds to the carbon already holding more H, giving the more stable secondary carbocation $\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{HCH}_3$, which takes up $\text{Br}^-$ → 2-bromopropane. 1-Bromopropane is the anti-Markovnikov product formed only with peroxide.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The peroxide (Kharasch) effect is observed in the addition of HBr to propene but not with HCl.
Reason (R): The H–Cl bond is too strong to be cleaved homolytically by the free radicals formed from the peroxide.

explanation.en: Anti-Markovnikov addition occurs by a free-radical chain in which H–Br is homolysed. The H–Cl bond (≈ 431 kJ mol⁻¹) is not broken by these radicals. (With HI, the iodine radicals combine to I₂ instead of adding.) R correctly explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Which alkene gives only propanone on reductive ozonolysis (O₃ followed by Zn/H₂O)?

explanation.en: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}{=}\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ is symmetric; each half becomes $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}{=}\text{O}$. 2-Methylpropene gives propanone + methanal; but-2-ene gives two ethanal; 2-methylbut-2-ene gives propanone + ethanal.

stem.en: An alkene $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}$ gives butan-2-one as the ONLY product on reductive ozonolysis. The alkene is:

explanation.en: Rejoining two $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ units through their C=O carbons gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2(\text{CH}_3)\text{C}{=}\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ = 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene. Oct-4-ene gives butanal; 2,5-dimethylhex-3-ene gives 2-methylpropanal; 3-methylhept-3-ene gives butan-2-one plus butanal.

stem.en: Ethene decolourises cold, dilute, alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent). The organic product is:

explanation.en: Cold dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ adds two –OH groups across the double bond: $\text{CH}_2{=}\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (glycol). The purple colour disappearing is a test for unsaturation. Hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves the C=C bond instead.

stem.en: 2-Methylpropene is heated with acidified KMnO₄. The products are:

explanation.en: The C=C bond is cleaved. $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}{=}$ becomes $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}{=}\text{O}$ (a ketone; no H to oxidise further), and $=\text{CH}_2$ becomes HCOOH, which is oxidised further to $\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Methanal is a product of reductive ozonolysis, not of hot acidic permanganate.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Ethyne is more acidic than ethene and ethane.
Reason (R): The sp-hybridised carbon of ethyne has 50% s-character, so it holds the bonding electron pair of the C–H bond more tightly.

explanation.en: Greater s-character makes the carbon more electronegative (sp > sp² > sp³: 50%, 33%, 25%). The C–H pair is drawn closer to C, H⁺ is released more easily and the acetylide anion is more stable. Hence HC≡CH > H₂C=CH₂ > CH₃–CH₃ in acidity. R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Propyne is warmed with dilute H₂SO₄ in the presence of HgSO₄. The product is:

explanation.en: Markovnikov addition of water gives the enol $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)}{=}\text{CH}_2$, which tautomerises to the ketone $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. Only ethyne gives an aldehyde (ethanal) by this route; all higher alkynes give ketones.

stem.en: When ethyne is passed through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K, the product is:

explanation.en: Three molecules undergo cyclic polymerisation: $3\,\text{HC}{\equiv}\text{CH} \xrightarrow{\text{red-hot Fe tube, 873 K}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6$. This links aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons.

stem.en: How many σ bonds are present in one molecule of benzene?

explanation.en: Benzene has 6 C–C σ bonds and 6 C–H σ bonds = 12 σ bonds, plus 3 π bonds (6 delocalised π electrons). Counting each Kekulé double bond as two σ bonds would wrongly give 15.

stem.en: In the nitration of benzene with a mixture of concentrated HNO₃ and H₂SO₄, the attacking electrophile is:

explanation.en: Sulphuric acid protonates nitric acid, which loses water: $\text{HNO}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightleftharpoons \text{NO}_2^+ + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+ + 2\text{HSO}_4^-$. The nitronium ion attacks the ring to form the arenium ion (σ-complex). Anions cannot act as electrophiles.

stem.en: Benzene reacts with ethanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃. The product is:

explanation.en: Friedel–Crafts acylation: $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl} + \text{AlCl}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C}{\equiv}\text{O}^+ + \text{AlCl}_4^-$; the acylium ion substitutes the ring to give $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ (acetophenone). Ethylbenzene would need ethyl chloride (alkylation); benzophenone needs benzoyl chloride.

stem.en: Which substituent on benzene directs an incoming electrophile to the meta position?

explanation.en: –NO₂ withdraws electrons (–I, –R), reducing electron density most at ortho and para positions, so attack occurs at meta. –OH and –CH₃ are activating o/p directors; –Cl is deactivating but still o/p directing. Other meta directors: –CN, –CHO, –COOH, –SO₃H.

stem.en:
Statement I: Chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic substitution more slowly than benzene.
Statement II: Chlorine is ortho/para directing because of its +R effect, although its −I effect deactivates the ring.

explanation.en: The strong −I effect of Cl lowers the overall electron density of the ring (slower reaction), while lone-pair donation (+R) makes ortho and para relatively richer than meta, so those positions are attacked. Halogens are the standard case of deactivating o/p directors.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: The correct order of reactivity towards electrophilic nitration is:

explanation.en: –OCH₃ donates electrons strongly by resonance; –CH₃ donates weakly by +I and hyperconjugation; –NO₂ withdraws strongly. Hence C₆H₅OCH₃ > C₆H₅CH₃ > C₆H₆ > C₆H₅NO₂.

stem.en: Which of the following statements about benzene is/are correct?

explanation.en: Resonance makes every C–C bond equal (139 pm, between C–C 154 pm and C=C 134 pm). Because addition would destroy the aromatic sextet, benzene prefers substitution, which preserves it. For the same reason it does NOT decolourise bromine water (unlike alkenes); bromination needs a Lewis acid catalyst.

options.en: All six C–C bonds have the same length, 139 pm
It undergoes substitution reactions more readily than addition reactions
It has six delocalised π electrons

stem.en: The enthalpy of hydrogenation of cyclohexene is −119 kJ mol⁻¹ and that of benzene is −208 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the resonance energy of benzene (in kJ mol⁻¹, as a positive number)?

explanation.en: Expected for three isolated C=C bonds: 3 × (−119) = −357 kJ mol⁻¹. Observed: −208 kJ mol⁻¹. Benzene is more stable by 357 − 208 = 149 kJ mol⁻¹ — its resonance (delocalisation) energy.

stem.en: The best way to prepare m-chloronitrobenzene from benzene is:

explanation.en: –NO₂ is meta-directing, so nitrating first and then chlorinating with a Lewis acid puts Cl meta. Chlorinating first gives o- and p-chloronitrobenzene (Cl is o/p directing). Cl₂ in UV light adds to benzene (forming C₆H₆Cl₆) rather than substituting.

options.en: Nitration, then treatment with Cl₂ in UV light
Chlorination with Cl₂ in UV light, then nitration

stem.en: Benzene is treated with 1-chloropropane in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃. The major product is:

explanation.en: AlCl₃ generates (or begins to generate) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2^+$, which undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to the more stable $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^+$. Attack by benzene gives mainly isopropylbenzene. n-Propylbenzene is better made by Friedel–Crafts acylation (propanoyl chloride) followed by reduction.

stem.en: Which of the following reactions give ethane as the main organic product?

explanation.en: (A) Wurtz: $2\text{CH}_3\text{Br} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_6$. (B) Decarboxylation of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COONa}$ gives $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$. (C) Kolbe electrolysis of propanoate couples two ethyl radicals to give butane, not ethane. (D) Catalytic hydrogenation gives ethane.

options.en: Sodium propanoate heated with soda lime
Kolbe electrolysis of aqueous sodium propanoate

stem.en: How many structurally isomeric alkenes have the formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$? (Do not count geometrical isomers separately.)

explanation.en: Straight chain: pent-1-ene, pent-2-ene. Branched (2-methylbutane skeleton): 2-methylbut-1-ene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene. The neopentane skeleton cannot carry a C=C. Total 5 (6 if cis/trans-pent-2-ene are counted separately).

stem.en: 10 mL of a gaseous hydrocarbon $\text{C}_x\text{H}_y$ required exactly 55 mL of oxygen for complete combustion and produced 40 mL of $\text{CO}_2$ (all volumes at the same temperature and pressure). What is the value of y?

explanation.en: By Gay-Lussac's law, volumes are in mole ratio. $\text{CO}_2$: $10x = 40 \Rightarrow x = 4$. $\text{O}_2$: $10(x + y/4) = 55 \Rightarrow 4 + y/4 = 5.5 \Rightarrow y = 6$. The hydrocarbon is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$ (e.g. buta-1,3-diene or a butyne).

stem.en: The major product of the addition of HBr to 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene is:

explanation.en: Protonation gives the secondary cation $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}{-}\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}{-}\text{CH}_3$. A 1,2-methyl shift converts it to the tertiary cation $(\text{CH}_3)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}{-}\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$, which captures $\text{Br}^-$ to give 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane. 2-Bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane is the unrearranged (minor) Markovnikov product.

stem.en: A hydrocarbon $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8$ gives a white precipitate with ammoniacal silver nitrate and, on warming with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$/$\text{HgSO}_4$, gives 3-methylbutan-2-one. The hydrocarbon is:

explanation.en: A precipitate with $[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$ needs an acidic $\equiv\text{C–H}$, so it is a terminal alkyne. Markovnikov hydration of $\text{HC}{\equiv}\text{C}{-}\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}{-}\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ = 3-methylbutan-2-one. Pent-1-yne would give pentan-2-one; pent-2-yne and the allene have no terminal ≡C–H.

stem.en: n-Hexane heated with anhydrous AlCl₃ and HCl gas mainly gives:

explanation.en: This is isomerisation: the straight chain rearranges to branched alkanes (2- and 3-methylpentane), which have higher octane numbers. Benzene requires aromatisation over Cr₂O₃/V₂O₅ at 773 K.

stem.en: The major product of the acid-catalysed dehydration of butan-2-ol is:

explanation.en: Loss of H₂O gives a secondary carbocation; loss of H⁺ from the CH₂ side gives the more substituted (more stable) alkene but-2-ene as the major product, with but-1-ene as the minor one. 2-Methylpropene would need a skeletal rearrangement, which does not occur here.

stem.en: Benzene reacts with ozone to form a triozonide, which on treatment with Zn/H₂O gives:

explanation.en: Each of the three C=C bonds of a Kekulé structure is cleaved, giving three $\text{OHC–CHO}$ (glyoxal) units. Zn prevents oxidation to oxalic acid (ethanedioic acid). This is one of the few addition reactions of benzene.

stem.en: Which of the following give a white precipitate with ammoniacal silver nitrate solution?

explanation.en: Only terminal alkynes have the acidic $\equiv\text{C–H}$ that forms insoluble silver acetylides: $\text{HC}{\equiv}\text{CH} \rightarrow \text{AgC}{\equiv}\text{CAg}$ and $\text{R–C}{\equiv}\text{C–H} \rightarrow \text{R–C}{\equiv}\text{C–Ag}$. But-2-yne has no terminal H; propene's $sp^2$ C–H is far too weakly acidic.

stem.en: Benzene reacts with chlorine in bright sunlight (UV) in the absence of a Lewis acid to give:

explanation.en: Under UV light chlorine adds (free-radical addition) across all three double bonds: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$ (BHC; the γ-isomer is gammexane/lindane). Substitution to chlorobenzene needs $\text{FeCl}_3$/$\text{AlCl}_3$ in the dark.
